content:
I'd like to announce Mathlib now has Verso docstrings enabled in a subset of files on an experimental basis.

Verso is a sublanguage of Lean for formatting text, and because it is integrated with Lean itself, we get nice features like syntax highlighting and (currently opt-in) code checking: if you write a ```lean block while doc.verso is enabled, Verso will actually check the code you wrote for correctness as your Lean file is elaborated, and so examples in your documentation won't silently break anymore.

Verso's basic syntax is very similar to Markdown, so you can generally continue to write just like you're used to. One noticeable difference: emphasized text is written using _underscores_, and strong text is written using *asterisks* (in Markdown these would be *single* and **double** asterisks, respectively). In fact, there are 1300 files where Verso and Markdown syntax are identical, and those are the files where we enabled the doc.verso option.

Note that doc-gen doesn't support Verso yet so all docstrings get converted back to Markdown before rendering in doc-gen: for now you'll see Verso's features in the editor or while compiling only.

I'll be working on getting more files migrated to Verso and ensuring nothing breaks during the translation from Markdown to Verso.

If you have any questons about Verso, please ask them in this thread or send me a DM!
